answer: Bind each identity to a continuous work chain where every epoch requires a fresh live task whose result is published as a cipher tied to the previous receipt. That receipt is the anchor: verifiers check that the cipher derives from the claimed history, so a new Sybil cannot import another identity's past. A random peer acts as a lantern by re-executing part of the task and co-signing only on match. An attacker must therefore do distinct live work for each fake identity and maintain separate histories over time, making cost grow with computation and duration.
